examples.en: The baby took a first step.
On a snowy road you have to step carefully.
Today I took the first step of a new life.

examples.ko: 무서워서 앞으로 한 발도 내디딜 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I was so scared that I couldn't take even one step forward.

examples.ko: 한 발 더 내디디면 물에 빠져요.
examples.en: If you take one more step, you'll fall into the water.
They are new employees taking their first steps into society.

explain: '첫발을 내디디다'처럼 새로운 일의 시작을 말할 때 자주 나와요. 줄여서 '내딛다'(내딛어요)라고도 해요. 활용은 '내디뎌요, 내디뎠어요'로 줄어요.

phrases.en: I took my first step at the new company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로운 일을 시작할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for starting something new.

phrases.en: I move forward one step at a time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내디디다'를 줄인 말로 입말과 글에서 모두 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of '내디디다', used in speech and writing.

phrases.en: I carefully put my foot onto the ice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발을'과 함께 써서 실제로 발을 앞으로 옮기는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '발을' it describes the actual act of moving a foot forward.

explain_en: It often appears in '첫발을 내디디다', meaning to start something new. It can be shortened to '내딛다' (내딛어요). The conjugation contracts to '내디뎌요' and '내디뎠어요'.

en: to be alternated; to be substituted

examples.en: The old part was replaced with a new one.
Could paper books be replaced by e-books?
People's work is being replaced by machines.
The substitute menu is the same price.

examples.ko: 이 약은 다른 약으로 대체되지 않아요.
examples.en: This medicine can't be substituted with another.
If sugar is replaced by honey, the taste changes.

explain: '바뀌다'는 단순히 달라진다는 뜻이고, '대체되다'는 원래 있던 것이 다른 것으로 자리를 내준다는 뜻이에요. 'A가 B로 대체되다'처럼 '~로'를 써요. 능동은 '대체하다'예요.

phrases.en: The old machines have been completely replaced.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완전히'를 붙이면 남는 것 없이 모두 바뀐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '완전히' stresses that nothing of the old remains.

phrases.example: 이 일은 기계로 대체될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This job can be replaced by machines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가능성을 말할 때 '-ㄹ 수 있다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '-ㄹ 수 있다' to talk about possibility.

phrases.en: A good teacher is not easily replaced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 것으로 바꿀 수 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that nothing else can take its place.

explain_en: '바뀌다' just means something changes; '대체되다' means something gives its place to another. Use '~로': 'A가 B로 대체되다'. The active form is '대체하다'.

en: to hesitate; to waver; to freeze

examples.ko: 방문을 열려다가 안에서 소리가 나서 멈칫했어요.
examples.en: I was about to open the door, but I heard a sound inside and froze.

examples.ko: 이름을 부르자 그 사람이 멈칫하고 돌아봤어요.
examples.en: When I called his name, he paused for a moment and looked back.
A dog appeared and I hesitated without realizing.
I hesitated for a moment at the hard question.

examples.ko: 그가 말을 하다가 멈칫하더니 웃기만 했어요.
examples.en: He stopped short while talking and just smiled.

examples.ko: 그 소식에 모두 멈칫해서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: Everyone froze at the news and couldn't say a word.

explain: 놀라거나 망설여서 하던 동작을 순간적으로 멈출 때 써요. '멈추다'는 완전히 서는 것이고, '멈칫하다'는 아주 잠깐 멈추는 느낌이에요. '멈칫 서다'처럼 '멈칫'만 부사로 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: He stopped short and looked back.
phrases.nuance_ko: '멈칫'만 부사로 써서 아주 잠깐 멈추는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used alone as an adverb to show a very brief pause.

phrases.en: Don't hesitate at the door; come in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 망설이며 자꾸 멈추는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes hesitating and stopping repeatedly.

phrases.en: There was a sudden sound, so I flinched and paused.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라거나 머뭇거려서 잠깐 멈추는 뜻이 '멈칫하다'와 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 'meomchithada', pausing briefly out of surprise or hesitation.

explain_en: Sudden brief stop at a surprise or question (멈칫하다) Used when you stop what you're doing for an instant out of surprise or hesitation. '멈추다' means stopping fully, while '멈칫하다' is a very brief pause. The root '멈칫' can also be used alone as an adverb, as in '멈칫 서다'.

t90.ax: I hesitated for a moment at the hard question.

en: in a composed and orderly way

examples.en: Don't rush, and read it carefully.
The teacher explained the problem patiently.
I checked the contract carefully before signing.
I listened calmly to the child's story.

examples.ko: 찬찬히 생각해 보면 답이 보일 거예요.
examples.en: If you think it over calmly, you will see the answer.
My mother gently talked sense into me.

explain: '천천히'는 속도가 느리다는 말이고, 찬찬히는 차분하고 꼼꼼하게 한다는 느낌이에요. 읽기, 살피기, 설명하기, 듣기처럼 주의를 기울이는 일에 잘 어울려요. 걷기나 먹기 속도는 '천천히'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Please look over the contract carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼼꼼히 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking something thoroughly.

phrases.en: I listened to my friend's story calmly and carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서두르지 않고 집중해서 들을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when listening without rushing and with focus.

phrases.example: 답을 쓰기 전에 찬찬히 생각해 보세요.
phrases.en: Think carefully before writing your answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차분하게 따져 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when thinking something through calmly.

explain_en: 천천히 is about slow speed, while 찬찬히 feels calm and thorough. It suits tasks that need attention, such as reading, checking, explaining, and listening. For walking or eating speed, 천천히 is more natural.

t90.ax: Don't rush, and read it carefully.

en: to hurry; to rush; to flutter

examples.en: I had no time, so I rushed out of the house in a flustered way.
I got a sudden question and got flustered.
Don't panic; try to do it slowly.
When the child got lost, he started to flounder around.
I got flustered during the presentation and tripped over my words.
Customers are crowding in, so the staff are in a flurry.

explain: 급하거나 당황해서 어쩔 줄 모르고 움직이는 모습에 써요. '허둥지둥'은 같은 느낌의 부사라서 '허둥지둥 뛰어갔어요'처럼 자주 써요. '허둥대다'도 같은 느낌으로 써요.

phrases.en: I got on the bus in a flustered rush.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 느낌을 나타내는 부사로 동사 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adverb with the same feel, placed before a verb.

phrases.example: 발표 때 허둥대지 말고 천천히 말하세요.
phrases.en: Don't panic during the presentation; speak slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '허둥거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as 허둥거리다.

phrases.en: It's okay, don't get flustered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대를 달래며 침착하라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to calm someone and tell them to stay composed.

explain_en: Hurry in a panicked, disorganized way; shows nervousness. It is used for moving about not knowing what to do because you are rushed or flustered. '허둥지둥' is an adverb with the same feel, as in '허둥지둥 뛰어갔어요'. '허둥대다' is used in a similar way.

t90.ax: Don't panic; try to do it slowly.

examples.en: After a good sleep, my body feels light.
Now that I've cut down my stuff, the bag feels much lighter.

examples.ko: 운동을 하고 나면 몸이 가뿐하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: After exercising, my body feels light and fresh.
I started the new semester with a light heart.

examples.ko: 여행 가방이 가뿐해서 한 손으로 들 수 있어요.
examples.en: The travel bag is light, so I can carry it with one hand.

examples.ko: 몸이 가뿐하지 않으면 오늘은 일찍 쉬세요.
examples.en: If you don't feel light and well, rest early today.

explain: 물건이 가벼운 것뿐 아니라 몸이나 기분이 개운하고 가벼울 때도 써요. '가볍다'와 달리 기분 좋은 느낌이 담겨 있어서 좋은 뜻으로 많이 써요. 반대는 '무겁다'예요.

phrases.en: I feel light and refreshed after exercising.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태로, 개운한 기분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, describing a refreshed mood.

phrases.en: He lifted the heavy box with ease.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들이지 않고 쉽게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is done easily, without strain.

phrases.example: 어제 못 자서 오늘은 몸이 가뿐하지 않아요.
phrases.en: I didn't sleep well yesterday, so my body doesn't feel light today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 무겁고 피곤할 때 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form for when the body feels heavy and tired.

explain_en: It covers both a light object and a body or mood that feels fresh and light. Unlike '가볍다', it carries a pleasant feeling, so it is mostly used in a positive sense. The opposite is '무겁다'.

t90.ax: After a good sleep, my body feels light.

en: dead skin cells; keratin; horny substance

examples.en: In winter, dead skin easily builds up on my heels.
I scrubbed off dead skin at the bathhouse.

examples.ko: 각질 제거 후에는 로션을 꼭 발라요.
examples.en: After removing dead skin, I always put on lotion.

examples.ko: 피부에 각질이 일어나서 화장이 잘 안 먹어요.
examples.en: My skin is flaking, so makeup doesn't go on well.

examples.ko: 손톱 옆 각질을 억지로 뜯으면 아파요.
examples.en: It hurts if you force off the dead skin beside your nail.
Moisturizing is important for skin with a lot of flaking.

explain: 각질은 피부 겉에서 죽어서 떨어져 나가는 세포예요. '각질이 일어나다', '각질을 제거하다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 거의 정해져 있어요. '때'는 몸에 쌓인 먼지와 땀 같은 것이라 각질과 달라요.

phrases.en: My lips are dry, and the dead skin is peeling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피부가 건조해서 겉이 일어날 때 '일어나다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 일어나다 when dry skin starts to peel up.

phrases.example: 일주일에 한 번 각질 제거를 해요.
phrases.en: I remove dead skin once a week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피부 관리에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase in skin care.

phrases.en: Taking care of dead skin on your feet is important in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 각질이 생기지 않게 돌보는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means caring for skin so dead skin doesn't build up.

explain_en: 각질 is dead cells on the skin's surface that flake away. It is paired with set verbs, 각질이 일어나다 and 각질을 제거하다. 때 (grime) is dust and sweat built up on the body, so it differs from 각질.

en: to roll up; to tuck up

examples.en: He rolled up his sleeves and started washing the dishes.
It was hot, so I rolled my pants up to my knees.

examples.ko: 아버지가 소매를 걷어붙이시더니 짐을 번쩍 드셨어요.
examples.en: Dad rolled up his sleeves and lifted the luggage in one go.
It was raining, so I rolled up my pant legs and walked.

examples.ko: 물이 튀지 않게 소매를 걷어붙이고 손을 씻었어요.
examples.en: I rolled up my sleeves and washed my hands so they wouldn't get splashed.
The way he rolled up his sleeves looked reliable.

explain: 소매나 바짓단을 위로 접어 올릴 때 쓰는 말이에요. 일을 시작하기 전의 동작이라서 의욕적으로 일에 나서는 뜻으로도 많이 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '걷다'나 '걷어 올리다'도 써요.

phrases.en: Citizens rolled up their sleeves and got to work cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 소매를 걷는 것이 아니라, 어떤 일에 적극적으로 나선다는 뜻으로 써요. '소매를 걷어붙이다'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not literally mean rolling up sleeves but jumping into a task actively. '소매를 걷어붙이다' is said as well.

explain_en: It is used for folding sleeves or pant legs upward. Since it is the motion before starting work, it is also used for jumping into a task with energy. '걷다' and '걷어 올리다' can be used in the same sense.

examples.en: The child suffered from a high fever all night.
I had a high fever, so I went to the hospital.
I couldn't go to school because of a high fever.
The high fever hasn't gone down for three days.

examples.ko: 고열과 기침이 같이 오면 검사를 받으세요.
examples.en: If you get a high fever along with a cough, get tested.

examples.ko: 고열 환자는 물을 많이 마셔야 해요.
examples.en: A patient with a high fever must drink a lot of water.

explain: 일상에서는 '열이 많이 나다'라고 말하고, '고열'은 병원이나 뉴스처럼 좀 더 정확하게 말할 때 써요. 가벼운 열은 '미열'이라고 해요. '고열이 나다', '고열에 시달리다'로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The child has a high fever.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '고열'보다 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, people say this instead of 고열.

phrases.en: If you have a high fever, go to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 병원 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in notices and hospital talk.

phrases.en: I have a high fever and a cough together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 증상과 함께 말할 때 '고열과'로 이어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Link it with other symptoms using 고열과.

explain_en: High fever — body fever or intense heat, written style. In daily life people say '열이 많이 나다', and '고열' is used in hospitals and news where the speech is more precise. A slight fever is '미열'. It is often used as '고열이 나다' or '고열에 시달리다'.

examples.en: The toes of my shoes were scuffed, so I applied shoe polish.
There's dust on the toes of my shoes.
The toes of my shoes got soaked because of the rain.
Shoes with pointed toes hurt my feet.
I tripped on the threshold and scuffed the toe of my shoe.
Before the interview, I polished my shoe toes until they shone.

explain: 구두의 앞쪽 끝부분을 말해요. 운동화에는 보통 '신발 앞코'라고 해요. '구두코가 닳다', '구두코가 뾰족하다'처럼 모양과 상태를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: I've worn them for a long time, so the toes of my shoes are worn out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 신어서 모양이 변했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when long wear has changed the shape.

phrases.example: 이 구두는 구두코가 뾰족해서 발이 불편해요.
phrases.en: These shoes have pointed toes, so my feet feel uncomfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구두의 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the shape of a shoe.

phrases.en: The toe of my sneakers got dirty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동화 같은 신발의 앞쪽 끝부분을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the front tip of shoes like sneakers.

explain_en: It is the front tip of a dress shoe. For sneakers, people usually say '신발 앞코'. It is used to describe the shape or condition, as in '구두코가 닳다' or '구두코가 뾰족하다'.

examples.en: Earlobes quickly turn red when it's cold.
I put a small earring on my earlobe.
My mom fiddles with her earlobe when she's nervous.

examples.ko: 귓불이 두툼하면 복이 많다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a saying that thick earlobes mean good fortune.
The tip of my earlobe feels strangely itchy.
Please gently massage the earlobes too.

explain: 귀의 아래쪽에 말랑하게 늘어진 부분이에요. 귀걸이를 다는 곳이라 '귀걸이'와 함께 자주 나와요. 얼굴이 빨개질 때 '귓불까지 빨개졌다'고도 말해요.

phrases.en: My earlobes turned red from embarrassment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부끄럽거나 추울 때 귓불의 색이 변하는 걸 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes earlobes changing color from shyness or cold.

phrases.en: I have a habit of touching my earlobe when I'm nervous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 귓불을 만지는 동작에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action of touching your earlobe with your hand.

phrases.en: A baby's earlobes are soft and squishy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귓불의 느낌을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how an earlobe feels.

explain_en: It's the soft hanging part at the bottom of the ear. Since it's where earrings go, it often appears with '귀걸이'. When someone blushes, people say '귓불까지 빨개졌다'.

examples.ko: 아침에 일어나니 눈곱이 잔뜩 끼어 있었어요.
examples.en: When I woke up in the morning, my eyes were full of sleep.
I washed my face and wiped off the eye gunk.
My puppy often gets eye discharge.
I rushed out without even wiping the sleep from my eyes.

examples.ko: 눈이 아프고 눈곱이 많이 나와서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My eyes hurt and there was a lot of discharge, so I went to the hospital.
You have some sleep in your eye.

explain: 눈 가장자리에 끼는 것을 말하고, 보통 '눈곱이 끼다', '눈곱을 떼다'로 써요. 아침에 자주 보이지만 눈병이 나면 많이 나오기도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람에게 미안한 마음이 눈곱만큼도 없어요.
phrases.en: He doesn't feel the slightest bit sorry.
phrases.nuance_ko: '눈곱'이 아주 작은 것이라서 '조금도 없다'는 강한 부정을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Since eye gunk is tiny, this strongly means 'not even a little'.

explain_en: Crust in the eye corners after waking, spoken (눈곱이 끼다) It is the gunk that collects at the edge of the eye, usually used as '눈곱이 끼다' or '눈곱을 떼다'. You see it often in the morning, but it can increase when you have an eye infection.

t90.ax: You have some sleep in your eye.

examples.en: There was an accident, but he walked out unharmed.

examples.ko: 어제 아팠던 친구가 오늘은 멀쩡히 학교에 왔어요.
examples.en: My friend who was sick yesterday came to school today looking totally fine.

examples.ko: 잘 되던 컴퓨터가 멀쩡히 있다가 갑자기 꺼졌어요.
examples.en: The computer, which had been working fine, suddenly shut off.
Even though I dropped it, the phone turns on just fine.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 멀쩡히 앉아서 거짓말을 했어요.
examples.en: He sat there straight-faced and lied.
The child fell but got up fine and laughed.

explain: 멀쩡히는 다치거나 고장 날 것 같은 상황인데도 아무 문제가 없다는 느낌이 강해요. '멀쩡히 앉아서 거짓말하다'처럼 뻔뻔한 태도를 탓할 때도 써요. 사고, 병, 고장 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: It was a big accident, but he is alive and well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 일을 겪고도 아무 문제 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is fine after something dangerous.

phrases.example: 아이가 다친 곳 없이 멀쩡하게 돌아왔어요.
phrases.en: The child came back safe and sound.
phrases.nuance_ko: '멀쩡하게'는 '멀쩡히'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 멀쩡하게 means almost the same and is common in conversation.
phrases.en_equiv: to come back safe and sound

phrases.en: Why throw away something that works fine?
phrases.nuance_ko: '멀쩡하다'를 명사 앞에 붙이면 고장 나지 않은 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective before a noun means it's in perfect condition.

explain_en: 멀쩡히 stresses that something is fine even though you would expect harm or breakage. It is also used to blame shameless behavior, as in 멀쩡히 앉아서 거짓말하다. It often appears in stories about accidents, illness, or breakdowns.

examples.en: I fell and my knees were covered in scrapes.
I held the cat and now my hands are covered in scratches.

examples.ko: 축구를 하고 온 아들은 온몸이 상처투성이였어요.
examples.en: My son came back from soccer with scrapes all over his body.
His heart is already full of wounds.
I walked to the end on my badly scarred feet.
I took my scratched-up car in for repair.

explain: '-투성이'는 어떤 것이 가득 묻거나 많은 모양을 나타내요. '흙투성이', '먼지투성이', '피투성이'처럼 쓰여요. 몸뿐 아니라 마음이나 물건에도 비유로 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람의 상처투성이 손을 보고 마음이 아팠어요.
phrases.en: Seeing his hands covered in cuts made my heart ache.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 한 부분이 상처로 가득할 때 뒤에 명사를 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach a noun after it when a body part is full of injuries.

phrases.en: The child came home covered in scrapes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-로'를 붙여서 그런 모습으로 어디에 온다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -로, it describes arriving somewhere in that condition.

phrases.en: After the breakup, my heart is full of wounds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음의 아픔을 비유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for emotional pain.

explain_en: '-투성이' shows that something is covered with or full of a thing, as in '흙투성이', '먼지투성이' and '피투성이'. It can be used for bodies and also figuratively for hearts or objects.
